architecture.title: Stage 1 at a glance
architecture.alt: C source flows through the Trace Engine, schema-2 JSON, TraceStore, then validated semantic evidence; Stage 2 consumes the qualified results.
architecture.caption: The parser does not execute C; the future Semantic Engine does not change what the recorder observed.

compilation.title: Compilation to observation
compilation.alt: Build config enters GCC; the debug binary is run under GDB with a linked allocation wrapper; a separate sanitized binary is available for a later diagnostic run.

checkpoint.title: GDB command and checkpoint lifecycle
checkpoint.alt: At a stopped PC the engine drains events and observes memory, then sends a tokened MI instruction step and awaits an asynchronous stop before recording an outcome.

nodes.label: Observed *stopped
lines: Stop ID, frame PC = next instruction

nodes.label: Drain telemetry · checkpoint
lines: Read stack and memory only while stopped

nodes.label: Wait for next *stopped
lines: Timeout, signal and exit handled separately

nodes.label: Retain event or gap
lines: Before PC, outcome, next PC if observed

stack.title: Frames and variable observations
stack.alt: A stop contains a frame-zero variable vector, optional bounded caller frame vectors, a separate global vector, and separately budgeted raw bytes.

heap.title: Heap lifetime, reuse and realloc
heap.alt: Malloc starts ID 1. Free ends ID 1. A later allocation at the same address receives ID 2. Successful realloc can create a linked new ID, but only event and lifetime evidence verifies the link.

nodes.label: malloc(A) → ID 1
lines: PID-local event sequence; first lifetime begins

nodes.label: free(A) → end ID 1
lines: Historical bytes never become live again

nodes.label: malloc(A) → ID 2
lines: Same numeric address, new identity; old pointer origin unknown

nodes.label: realloc(ID 2) → ID 3
lines: Only corroborated event + lifetime link is definite

metadata.title: Static metadata versus observed runtime
metadata.alt: GCC DWARF describes compiled types and declarations; optional Clang AST describes syntax; GDB observes stopped runtime; fusion only records bounded candidate links.

records.title: DebugSessionTrace relationships
records.alt: A top-level trace contains snapshots, disassembly and instruction events, gaps and source checkpoints, heap records and lifetimes, and independent tool reports.

ownership.title: One trace, many borrowed readers
ownership.alt: TraceStore holds an Arc of the canonical trace and an Arc of position indexes; borrowed views and trace-scoped EvidenceRef resolve to those original records.

confidence.title: Validation and confidence are different gates
confidence.alt: Deserialization checks schema; opt-in deep validation detects structural corruption or partial/unavailable evidence; confidence qualifies each relationship; Stage 2 interprets without inventing observations.

consumer.title: TP-6 and TP-7 consumer path
consumer.alt: A single validated view holds the report and borrows the store; checkpoint summary and bounded pages provide trace-scoped references and qualified events without copying records.

partial.title: From failure to qualified partial evidence
partial.alt: GDB timeout, trace-byte cap or missing child ACK keeps whatever records were safely observed; coverage and stage status mark the missing scope; the parser reports partial or unavailable, not fabricated success.

nodes.label: Retain observed prefix
lines: Snapshots, events and diagnostics if available

nodes.label: Validate and downgrade
lines: Partial ≠ structural corruption; links may be unavailable

handoff.title: Stage 1 → downstream boundary
handoff.alt: Stage 1 gives validated borrowed evidence and bounded pages; downstream consumers must preserve observation scope and uncertainty.

stage1-system.title: Production tools and the Stage 1 boundary
stage1-system.alt: GCC builds a debug binary; GDB observes it while an allocation wrapper writes a separate file. Clang syntax, Valgrind and sanitizer diagnostics are optional or independent. The engine emits schema-2 JSON to the parser and borrowed consumer views.
stage1-system.caption: Solid edges transfer artifacts or observations. Dashed edges are optional or independent runs; Valgrind and sanitizers do not observe the GDB process.

engine-subsystems.title: Trace Engine production subsystem groups
engine-subsystems.alt: Configuration and supervision control compilation and GDB recording. C wrapper events and metadata flow to the trace; independent diagnostic passes contribute separate reports before JSON export.
engine-subsystems.caption: Groups are architectural dependencies and data transfers, not an exhaustive Rust function-call graph. The C wrapper crosses a file boundary.

parser-subsystems.title: Trace Parser ownership and query layers
parser-subsystems.alt: JSON decoder gates schema, then TraceStore owns a canonical Arc and position indexes. Borrowed views and deep validation feed confidence-qualified TP-6 and paged TP-7 consumers; journals are parsed as records separately.
parser-subsystems.caption: Load does not imply deep validation. The journal path has no arrow to a reconstructed TraceStore.

module-dependencies.title: Major module dependency and data paths
module-dependencies.alt: CLI invokes trace orchestration. Compiler and debugger data cross through models and recording; evidence fusion references static metadata; parser indexing and validation borrow the canonical trace before consumer queries.
module-dependencies.caption: Architectural data/dependency map: for verified individual calls use the interactive explorer. No edge from parser back into the live GDB process.

runtime-lifecycle.title: Typical engine recording lifecycle
runtime-lifecycle.alt: After configuration the engine compiles and starts GDB; stopped-state capture and heap collection repeat under budgets; separate diagnostics run conditionally; DWARF association, evidence fusion and final JSON export complete the trace.
runtime-lifecycle.caption: Sanitizer and Valgrind ordering depends on trigger and deadline; static extraction and association are distinct operations. See trace.rs for conditional branches.

engine-parser-flow.title: Engine-to-Parser serialization boundary
engine-parser-flow.alt: Observed runtime, metadata and independent reports form DebugSessionTrace. Final JSON is exported, decoded and gated by schema, indexed in one TraceStore, then optionally deep-validated for borrowed consumer views.

nodes.label: Observed and static records
lines: Snapshots, events, DWARF, optional AST, reports

nodes.label: DebugSessionTrace (schema 2)
lines: Owned engine model; no guessed missing fields

identity-domains.title: Distinct identity domains and candidate bridges
identity-domains.alt: TraceStore owner distinguishes equal documents. Snapshot position, stop ID, attempted and retained instruction positions, activation and variable identity, PID and allocation lifetime are separate runtime domains. DWARF and AST IDs are static and source-site matches only candidates.
identity-domains.caption: Dashed bridges are correlations/candidates, not identity proofs. Allocation ID is verified from event and lifetime records, never address equality.

resource-failure.title: Different limits at different boundaries
resource-failure.alt: Whole-session deadline and resource caps constrain the engine; stop-loop, journal and export budgets act separately. Parser input/validation limits and paged consumer errors are different boundaries; missing observations reach consumers as qualified uncertainty.
resource-failure.caption: Solid arrows show propagation of retained partial evidence; dashed arrows denote distinct controls, not a single shared RAM guarantee.

public-consumer.title: Approved Stage 1 consumer boundary
public-consumer.alt: A loaded immutable TraceStore supplies original records and shared indexes; explicit deep validation gives a report; TP-6 qualifies relationships and TP-7 returns bounded borrowed pages. Downstream consumers preserve those statuses.
public-consumer.caption: A successful schema load is not evidence validity; source-site candidates and independent reports do not turn into exact primary-run IDs.
